seoTitle: Mara Region Tanzania — Serengeti Safari Guide 2026
intro: The Mara Region in northern Tanzania is home to the Serengeti National Park, one of the world's most celebrated wildlife destinations and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Covering over 30,000 square kilometres of open savanna, woodland, and riverine forest, the Serengeti ecosystem supports the largest terrestrial mammal migration on earth — over 1.5 million wildebeest, 200,000 zebra, and 300,000 gazelle moving in an endless clockwise circuit through Tanzania and Kenya.

sections.heading: The Great Wildebeest Migration
sections.content: The Serengeti's defining spectacle is the annual Great Migration — the largest movement of land animals on the planet. The herds follow rainfall and fresh grass in a circular route: calving season on the southern plains (January–February), the long northward trek through the western corridor (May–July), river crossings at the Mara River in the north (July–October), and the return south (November–December). The Mara River crossings are the most dramatic episode — crocodiles ambush the herds as hundreds of thousands of animals plunge into the water simultaneously. No two crossings are the same, and witnessing one is widely considered the greatest wildlife event on earth.

sections.heading: Wildlife Beyond the Migration
sections.content: The Serengeti's year-round resident population is extraordinary even without the Migration. The park holds one of Africa's highest densities of lion — an estimated 3,000 individuals across multiple prides. Leopard are regularly seen in the kopjes (granite outcrops) of the central Seronera area. Cheetah hunt on the open plains of the south. Elephant, buffalo, giraffe, hippo, crocodile, wild dog, hyena, jackal, and over 500 bird species round out one of the continent's richest ecosystems. The Grumeti Reserve, bordering the western Serengeti, offers exclusive Big Five game viewing with far fewer vehicles.

sections.heading: Best Time to Visit the Serengeti
sections.content: The Serengeti is a year-round destination, but timing determines what you see. January to March is calving season — the southern plains fill with tens of thousands of newborn wildebeest, drawing predators in numbers rarely seen elsewhere. May to June offers the spectacle of the herds moving north through the western corridor, with the Grumeti River crossings beginning. July to October is peak season in the north — the Mara River crossings happen repeatedly as the herds mill back and forth. November and December see the migration return south as the short rains bring fresh grass. The dry season (June–October) offers the best general game viewing: grass is short, animals concentrate at water sources, and roads are passable everywhere.

sections.heading: How to Get to Mara Region
sections.content: The primary entry point for the Serengeti is by small aircraft from Arusha or Kilimanjaro. Scheduled and chartered flights land at multiple airstrips inside the park (Seronera, Kogatende, Grumeti, Lobo). By road, the Serengeti is 335 kilometres west of Arusha — approximately 6–8 hours by 4x4 through Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Most visitors combine a road safari through Ngorongoro with the Serengeti. Fly-in safaris are faster and more expensive but allow you to reach the remote northern Kogatende area (near the Mara River) that road vehicles rarely access.

sections.heading: Safari Camps and Lodges
sections.content: The Serengeti has accommodation ranging from public campsites ($35/person/night) to ultra-luxury mobile tented camps that follow the Migration ($1,500+/person/night). The central Seronera area has mid-range lodges with reliable Big Five sightings year-round. The northern sector around Kogatende offers the best Migration viewing in July–October but is remote and expensive. The western corridor (Grumeti area) is less visited but excellent for May–June Migration action. For most first-time visitors, a combination of central Seronera camp plus one night in the north delivers the best value and experience.

sections.heading: Combining Serengeti with Other Parks
sections.content: The Mara Region sits in Tanzania's Northern Circuit — the most popular safari route in Africa. A classic 7-day itinerary combines Tarangire National Park (elephants, baobab), Ngorongoro Crater (densest wildlife concentration on earth), and the Serengeti. Add Olduvai Gorge for palaeontology context. The lesser-known Ikorongo Game Reserve, adjacent to the western Serengeti, offers walking safaris and night drives not permitted inside the national park. Kenya's Masai Mara, across the northern border, is the same ecosystem — a cross-border safari combining both is possible with the right operator.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see the Great Migration in the Serengeti?
faqs.a: The Migration is present in the Serengeti year-round. For river crossings at the Mara River (the most dramatic moment), visit July to October. For calving season on the southern plains, January to March. There is no bad time — the herds are always somewhere in the ecosystem.

faqs.q: How much does a Serengeti safari cost?
faqs.a: Budget safaris run $150–250/person/day (shared vehicle, public campsite). Mid-range camps run $300–500/person/day. Luxury tented camps cost $600–1,500+/person/day. Park fees alone are $70/person/day. A 5-day mid-range Serengeti safari typically costs $1,500–2,500 per person all-inclusive.

faqs.q: Can I do a self-drive safari in the Serengeti?
faqs.a: Yes, self-drive is permitted. You need a 4x4 with high clearance, a valid driving licence, and a pre-booked campsite or lodge. Navigation is straightforward with offline maps. However, an experienced guide dramatically improves wildlife sightings — guides know where predators have been feeding and where the Migration is moving.

faqs.q: Is the Serengeti safe to visit?
faqs.a: Yes. The Serengeti National Park is one of the safest wildlife destinations in Africa for visitors. Tanzania has a stable political environment, and the park is well-managed by TANAPA. The main risks are animal encounters if you exit your vehicle — never walk outside a designated area without a guide.

faqs.q: How many days do I need in the Serengeti?
faqs.a: Minimum 3 nights to cover the central and southern areas. 5–7 nights if you want to reach the northern Mara River area and see the Migration crossings. Most visitors combine the Serengeti with 2 nights at Ngorongoro and 1–2 nights at Tarangire for a 7–10 day Northern Circuit safari.

tips: Book river crossing camps 6–12 months in advance for July–September — availability is extremely limited
Fly into the northern Kogatende airstrip for Mara River crossings — road access takes a full day
Early morning game drives (06:00–10:00) produce 80% of predator sightings
Bring a telephoto lens (400mm minimum) — animals in the open plains are often far from the vehicle
The southern plains in February are less visited but offer spectacular predator-prey action during calving
Budget extra for park fees — $70/person/day adds up quickly on a 7-day trip
